practices.practice: Create a vector index with the MongoDB createIndexes command using key: { <path>: "cosmosSearch" } and set cosmosSearchOptions.kind to one of vector-hnsw, vector-ivf, or vector-diskann and supply algorithm parameters (dimensions, m, efConstruction, numLists, similarity, etc.).
practices.prior_belief: For vector search, store embeddings in a single array field (e.g., embedding) and create a vector index with explicit algorithm and parameters (algorithm: hnsw or diskann; set dims equal to embedding length and tune m/efConstruction or nlist/ef as supported). Record the index name and algorithm parameters in code or infra so they can be recreated deterministically.

practices.practice: Perform vector similarity searches with the $search aggregation stage using the cosmosSearch operator (provide vector, path and k; optionally efSearch) and project the $meta "searchScore" to get the similarity score and returnStoredSource to retrieve the document.

practices.practice: Ensure vectors are stored as a number[] (numeric array) and note that indexing applies to only one vector per path and only one vector index can exist per vector path.

practices.practice: Choose the vector algorithm based on scale and memory tradeoffs (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN) and tune algorithm parameters (HNSW: m and efConstruction; search-time efSearch; IVF: numLists and nProbes; DiskANN: maxDegree/lBuild and product quantization options).

practices.practice: For IVF indexes, set numLists relative to dataset size (recommendation: numLists = documentCount/1000 for up to 1M docs; use larger numLists as data grows) and tune nProbes at query time to trade off latency and recall.

practices.practice: To prefilter vector searches (preserve top-k recall), create a standard index on the filter property in addition to the vector index and include a filter clause in the cosmosSearch query rather than post-filtering results.

practices.practice: Reuse a single MongoClient per process (share the MongoClient across requests) rather than creating a new client for every request; the drivers and samples explicitly reuse one client/pool per application.

practices.prior_belief: Use TLS/SSL and lock down network access for the cluster: require TLS in the connection string (ssl=true or tls=true), restrict allowed client IP ranges, and use firewall rules or VNet integration / private endpoints rather than exposing the cluster widely.

practices.prior_belief: Restrict account keys and use least-privilege accounts / roles where available: use a read-only account for screening queries and a separate write/admin account for seeding and index creation; rotate credentials periodically.

practices.practice: Use explain()/explain("executionStats") and query-plan inspection to verify index usage and to identify when queries are causing collection scans; use the explain output to guide index creation.

practices.practice: Normalize text for search using analyzers/token filters (lowerCase, asciiFolding, patternReplace) and/or materialize normalized fields (lowercased, ASCII-folded, punctuation removed) in indexed fields so queries can use the index rather than normalizing only at query time.
practices.prior_belief: Use consistent normalization before storing and searching names (lowercasing, removing punctuation, Unicode NFKC, ASCII folding) and store the normalized value in an indexed field rather than normalizing only at query time.

practices.practice: Avoid unbounded full-collection regex scans in production; prefer indexed filters, text/search indexes, custom analyzers (edgeGram / n-gram), or scope regex with prefilters (country, partition key) to limit candidate sets.
practices.prior_belief: For fuzzy name matching, avoid expensive full-collection regex scans in production; instead either (a) maintain a text index and use text search for tokens, (b) store tokenized n-grams in an indexed array field and query those, or (c) scope regex searches with a prefilter (e.g., country or name length) to limit candidate set.

practices.practice: Instrument cluster and queries: enable diagnostic logs and monitoring (CPU, memory, IOPS), capture query latencies and candidate counts for vector queries, and use those metrics to tune index algorithm parameters (ef, m, nlist) and scaling decisions.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor query latencies, RU consumption per operation, and index size. Capture metrics for vector search (latency, candidate counts) so you can tune index algorithm parameters (ef, m, nlist) and provisioned throughput appropriately.

practices.practice: Scale the cluster's compute tier (cluster tier like M30+) and storage when vector indexes need more memory or compute rather than relying on Cosmos-style RU autoscale; DocumentDB uses cluster tiers and compute scaling to handle vector-index resource needs.

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient faults, add jitter, limit retries, and ensure writes are idempotent (use idempotent upserts or tokens) before retrying; avoid retrying non-idempotent multi-document transactions blindly.

practices.practice: Use TTL only for ephemeral or test data; do not enable TTL for canonical, authoritative data (like a canonical sanctions list) unless you intend that data to expire.

notes:
I inspected the app files to identify the areas it touches (connection pooling, env var secrets, createIndexes vector index script, $search+cosmosSearch pipeline, regex queries, seeding, embeddings, projections). I then searched Microsoft documentation for DocumentDB vector search, indexing, security, auth, monitoring, and query optimization. Where Microsoft docs explicitly state a practice it is recorded as found_in_public_source; prior beliefs were compared and marked confirmed, contradicted, or left as prior_knowledge_only when no DocumentDB doc was found. Several prior beliefs drawn from general MongoDB or Cosmos practices (embedding metadata, n-gram array advice, idempotent index-creation error handling, configurable normalization and tie-break rules) had no direct DocumentDB documentation and were recorded as prior_knowledge_only with the queries I tried listed above.
